rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -n "" curriculum/lectures/the-loop-has-a-name.md confirms line text. chunk 1 line 7 "The thing you built at M5" and "The checks you just ranked against your dominant gap" resolve against this module's own prior beats: verified live against curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md line 57 (include-link places this lecture after the module's own exercise) and curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md lines 17-33 (Phase 1: diff the two sessions, rank the gaps, dominant gap named) — module-arc-beat carve-out. chunk 1 line 10 "on the map they are the checking loop the M2 drawing left dashed, now drawn solid" — verified the M2 module (plan-mode-done-right.md) includes the-whole-map.md (grep -rln the-whole-map curriculum/trainings/ shows plan-mode-done-right.md), and the-whole-map.md line 119 shows the dashed checking loop tag; arc-earned spine vocabulary, self-cashing. chunk 2 line 15 "Naming it is what lets you reuse it" resolves to "the shape"/"the primitive" named in chunk 2's own line 14. chunk 3 line 20 "Read that as your verifier from M5, scaled" resolves to the Intercom numbers in the same chunk's line 19. chunk 5 line 32 "The three pieces (reference, plan, verifier)" and "the encode loop you ran at M6" self-define via their own parentheticals. Closer line 35 "That is the flywheel" defines the term in the same sentence.

Harm check: this rule prevents a reader from being stranded resolving a claim they'd have to guess which file/position it points at; absent here. chunk 1's "M5"/"M2 drawing" and chunk 5's "M6" name the source module directly and unpack the claim in the same clause (e.g. line 7 "The thing you built at M5 reads an agent's work and decides whether it meets a bar"), rather than pointing at another file by bare position ("the opening lecture said"). No file referenced by position alone.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal demo instruction anywhere in the body (grep -niE "guess|predict" against the file returns no body hits above line 37); this is a consolidation/naming closer, not a live-demo beat, so no harm this rule guards against can occur.
All five ## chunks carry 2-4 substantive bullets each with a self-carrying claim (verified against grep -n "" line dump above); no wait-state or single context-dependent bullet slide.

Each header is a true (not contradicted) summary of its chunk: "Eval" names the term chunk 1 defines; "One primitive, placed wherever there's a bar" matches chunk 2's reuse/placement content; "The eval primitive scales unchanged" matches chunk 3's Intercom-scale argument and its closing line 21; "The primitive that runs on cadence" matches chunk 4's scheduling content; "Why the loop survives the model" matches chunk 5's stance-not-tooling argument. Chunk 0's H1 states the lecture's thesis and its lede sets up the recognition beat the following chunks unpack — not contradicted by content, consistent with this corpus's thesis-first closer convention.

No "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction anywhere in body (grep -n "Not " the file returns no hits). chunk 5 line 32's "Reference because...Plan because...Verifier because...Encode because..." is a four-part enumeration but every leg carries distinct, new concrete content (agent forgets / window fills / plausible-but-wrong failure mode / lesson re-learned) rather than hollow repetition — not the banned tic shape. No self-grading superlatives (grep -niE "one of the most|most useful|most important" returns no hits). No number-with-own-retraction pattern — chunk 3's Intercom numbers (line 19) are stated plainly with self-report attribution, no "could be more, could be less" hedge. No abstraction-noun stack left uncashed — chunk 5's "a stance toward a thing that does not behave deterministically" (line 32) is immediately cashed into four concrete reasons in the same sentence. No verb triplet with an empty leg.
